thread.title: Blue Chips Rule the Market Despite Headwinds | Investopedia

title: Blue Chips Rule the Market Despite Headwinds | Investopedia
text:
Blue Chips Rule the Market Despite Headwinds By Mark Kolakowski | Updated October 3, 2018 — 1:00 PM EDT
Blue chip stocks in Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) and S&P 500 (SPX) have become the undisputed winners in the market. They outpaced all other asset classes in the latest quarter and are off to a good start this month, despite a host of trends that may curb future gains including rising interest rates, increasing trade conflicts and slowing global economic growth. The largest of the blue chips did the best. "Performance was better up the cap spectrum 3Q," strategists at Bank of America Merrill Lynch (BofAML) wrote in a recent report, adding, "within the S&P 500, mega caps dominated, with the Nifty 50 [i.e., the 50 largest by market cap ] outperforming both the Not-so-Nifty 450 by over 1 ppt [percentage point]." The table below illustrates the difference in performance for leading market indexes, by size category. The Nasdaq Composite includes over 3,300 stocks, and thus straddles size categories.
Blue Chip Stocks Are Winning Index
Sources: Bank of America Merrill Lynch Significance For Investors
"We expect large caps to continue to outperform, and recommend tilting up the cap spectrum," BofAML says. They note that, for the month of September, the third quarter, and the year-to-date (YTD), U.S. stocks outperformed other asset classes such as government bonds, corporate bonds, cash and gold. Among equities, they add that U.S. large caps have outperformed non-U.S. stocks. The table below compares total returns (dividends and interest included) for key asset classes in the third quarter.
Large Cap Stocks Rule The Market Asset Category 0.5%
Source: Bank of America Merrill Lynch
Within the S&P 500, 8 of the 11 sectors were up in the third quarter, indicating good market breadth . Growth stocks outperformed value stocks , and high quality stocks ( credit rating of B+ or better) outperformed low quality stocks (rating of B or less). As evidence that investors are seeking safety and stability, the highest quality stocks of all (those with A+ ratings) were the best performers overall in September and in the third quarter, but only second-best on a YTD basis. Interestingly, they are beaten on a YTD basis by the lowest quality stocks of all (ratings of C or D).
BofAML also looked at key metrics that indicate quality, such as return on equity (ROE) , return on assets (ROA) , and return on capital (ROC) . Stocks scoring high on these quality factors outperformed stocks scoring high on all other factors that BofAML tracks.
As indicated in the first table above, the Dow Jones Industrial Average performed even better than the S&P 500 in the third quarter, up 9.0% versus 7.2%. Among the 30 Dow stocks, the top 5 gainers were, per Investor's Business Daily : Apple Inc. ( AAPL ), +22%, Walgreens Boots Alliance Inc. ( WBA ), +21.5%, Pfizer Inc. ( PFE ), +21.5%, Merck & Co. Inc. ( MRK ), +16.9%, and Microsoft Corp. ( MSFT ), +16%. Looking Ahead
While the large caps have largely shrugged off concerns about tariffs and trade wars, this remains a major risk for the group. Many members of the S&P 500 are highly globalized companies, heavily reliant on sales abroad and on imported materials, components and finished goods. A recent report from Goldman Sachs suggests that investors look to companies with high profit margins and proven pricing power , as a defensive measure. (For more, see also: 10 High-Margin Stocks To Survive The U.S.-China Trade War .)
Meanwhile, Jim Paulsen, chief investment strategist at The Leuthold Group, notes that the most defensive sectors of the S&P 500 have been market leaders lately, and that troubles him. Based on his analysis of history, he sees this as a signal of an upcoming recession and stock market drop. (For more, see also: Why Stock Market's 'Out of Whack' Leadership Signals Next Crash .)
